evals.name: should-trigger-pr-review-comment
evals.prompt: Write a PR review comment for this change — I want to ask the author to split the validation logic from the UI wiring before approving.
evals.expected_behavior: Activates comment-writer. Reads voice rules and applies the comment formula (observation -> why -> next action). Returns a short, direct comment in English (or matches whatever language the author's PR uses) without em-dashes, without 'I'd like to', without filler praise. Includes the technical reason for the split so the author does not have to guess. Offers an A/B variant only if there are two reasonable phrasings (more direct vs more diplomatic).

evals.name: should-trigger-spanish-issue-reply
evals.prompt: Redactar respuesta para issue UPEX-300 — el reporter dice que no puede reproducir, pero yo sí pude. Quiero contarle el repro y pedirle que confirme.
evals.expected_behavior: Activates comment-writer. Detects Spanish thread and uses Rioplatense voseo (`podés`, `fijate`, `dale`). Applies the formula: open with the repro fact, follow with the conditions (Chrome version, cookie state, etc.), close with the explicit ask ('confirmame que reproducís así también'). No em-dashes. No 'I'd like to' or its Spanish equivalents. Sounds like a teammate, not support.

evals.name: should-trigger-nitpick-wording
evals.prompt: How should I word this nitpick? The helper at line 42 could move to utils/format.ts but it's not a blocker.
evals.expected_behavior: Activates comment-writer. Frames the comment as a non-blocking nit explicitly ('Nit (non-blocking):' or equivalent), states the concrete observation, gives the reason (other files import the same pattern), and signals it is OK to merge as-is. Keeps it under 3 short lines. Avoids hedging that would make the author treat the nit as a request for change.

evals.name: should-trigger-spanish-rejection-explanation
evals.prompt: Escribir el comentario explicando el rejection del PR — el approach está bien pero el alcance se fue de scope, hay que cerrarlo y partir en dos PRs nuevos.
evals.expected_behavior: Activates comment-writer. Spanish, voseo Rioplatense. Opens with the decision (cierre del PR), gives the reason (scope creep concreto: qué archivos están fuera del ticket original), y propone el next step (2 PRs nuevos con scope acotado, sugerencia de cómo partirlos). Tono firme pero cálido — no suena a rejection automático ni a soporte. Sin em-dashes, sin 'I'd like to', sin praise vacía.

evals.name: should-not-trigger-commit-message
evals.prompt: Write the commit message for this change — I refactored the auth middleware to use the new token validator.
evals.expected_behavior: Does NOT activate comment-writer. Commit messages follow a different convention (semantic prefixes, imperative mood, line-length rules) and live under /git-flow-master. Should route to /git-flow-master or the project's commit-message guidance. comment-writer is for human-to-human conversational artifacts, not git metadata.

evals.name: should-not-trigger-marketing-email
evals.prompt: Draft the marketing email announcing the new feature to our customers.
evals.expected_behavior: Does NOT activate comment-writer. Customer-facing marketing copy has different goals (persuasion, brand voice, conversion) and audience (customers, not teammates). Should route to a copywriting workflow. comment-writer is for internal collaboration comments where the goal is fast, useful feedback between developers.
